equivalent_efficiency.method: Divide modeled drag power plus measured climb power (zero in level flight) by shaft power. Shaft BHP comes from the trial or the stated proxy. Uses the existing clean or climb drag and quasi-steady climb. Related fitted data cannot be independent eta validation.

p47b.condition: 41-5902 torque-meter BHP, true speed, 12565 lb. Donor interpolation is within P-47C source density ratios. J, Cp and tip Mach differences remain visible. No inferred correction for IAS across installations.
p47b.comparison_basis: equivalent_eta keeps the full calibrated model drag. propeller_comparison shows the alternative of assigning the explicit fitted power-proportional term entirely to useful power and keeping the fitted fixed area term. These are two allocations of the same power balance. The physical allocation requires independent evidence.

paired_propeller_swaps.conditions: One specimen and campaign, same reported climb TAS, torque BHP, weight and open cooling. Convert climb-rate difference to equivalent useful-power change; propeller slipstream drag is included in this installed effect.

reference_values.rule: Use 80% as the fixed shaft-to-useful-power starting value. At the documented Curtiss 714 P-47B military climb condition, use 76% and one fixed open-cooling drag area.
reference_values.basis: 80% is Greg’s provisional constant. 76% rounds the average of the three close military-climb matches to NACA L4L07 at 5000, 10000 and 12600 ft. Values transferred to another installation are calculated reference inputs.
reference_values.p47b_military_level_basis: The high-load Curtiss runs 24-5 and 24-2 give 0.801 and 0.759. The 41-5902 level checks support holding the rounded 0.76 through its high-altitude test points. Interpolate within the two nodes and hold the nearest endpoint over the checked P-47B domain.

flight_efficiency.method: The 80% constant comes from Greg’s worksheet. Compare it and the current momentum/loss equation at each NACA test’s J, Cp and helical tip Mach. The two reports have separate installations.

summaries.id: fast flight, J 1.55–2.15 and tip Mach 0.94–1.02

working_reference.level_method: Condition both calculations on the same shaft power and weight. The 80% model sets one clean drag coefficient from the designated speed anchor. The other rows check the transfer. Induced drag uses the existing geometry and e.
working_reference.climb_method: Hold the 80% level drag reference and fit one nonnegative added drag area at the named climb anchor. In the P-47B military replay use the 76% same-blade transfer. Test on the common rows excluded from the older fit and the separate P-47B airframe.

p38g_part_power.method: Interpolate within each original level speed versus chart BHP series, using adjacent remaining points to check each held-out interior point. Original RPM, mass and BHP are retained. Useful power is conditional on the 80% reference value.

input.cooling: Clean for level, acceleration and turn. Existing climb cooling at each climb state.
input.interpretation: Deterministic stress sweep. Each state changes only useful power, capped at shaft power. No fit or probability weighting. Outer factors may exceed the ideal disk or actual blade limits.
input.indexing: Every result array within a case follows output_factors. The at_eas entries identify each EAS slice.
input.timed_acceleration: Constant-altitude, fixed-mass integral over the specified EAS interval using the corresponding TAS steps. Starts at the selected rating. No rating changes or fuel burn.
input.missing: Unavailable rating-altitude cases and null values indicate unsupported power, provisional stall, absent high-speed crossing, insufficient power to reach the timed target or no sustained turn.
